method: The owner pasted a real Foundry resource key into Cursor IDE. Each test sent one short prompt from a new Agent chat. A request counts as 'reached' only if Foundry or the proxy recorded it. Server side: Azure Monitor metrics for each deployment plus a temporary Log Analytics diagnostic sink (RequestResponse and AzureOpenAIRequestUsage categories). Proxy side: scripts/foundry_claude_proxy.py logs every request it receives, including rejected ones. Client side: scripts/summarize_cursor_agent_log.py over Cursor's local agent-host log. UI messages are quoted as shown. Hosts, keys and ids are not published; the tunnel and the diagnostic sink were deleted afterwards.

key_validation.check: The key Cursor stored (read from its local encrypted settings) was compared on this machine with the resource's Key2; they were identical. Only the yes/no result was printed; the key itself is not recorded.
key_validation.same_key_direct_calls: 200 on the legacy Azure chat route for the GPT deployments, 200 on /openai/v1/chat/completions and /openai/v1/responses for GPT; Claude 200 on Responses and on /anthropic/v1/messages with x-api-key (key-route-probe.json)

reading: With a valid key, existing deployments and a proxy that answers through a public tunnel, Cursor IDE 3.30.14 on this account sent no request to Foundry or to the proxy in seven tests. Cursor's own log shows each turn handed to its backend, which returned resource_exhausted for the Azure slot and unauthenticated for the OpenAI override before any outbound call was seen. Wrong keys and wrong api-version values are invisible in Foundry metrics and logs, so an Azure-side rejection cannot be fully excluded for tests A, C, D and E; it can be excluded for B, F and F2, where the proxy logs every request. The cause inside Cursor is not visible from outside. Other users report the same slot working, so the result may depend on account, plan or version.
